user_problem: I allocate 3 worker slots from instance types {cpu, gpu, mem}, and I can pick the same type more than once. Which allocation mixes are safe for batch vs serving, and how do diversity and cost trade off?
bundle_offer: Bundle models the allocation as FW_CombiR(3): a size-3 MULTISET over the instance types (repetition allowed) crossed with the workload class; a resource-mix oracle flags zero-diversity (single point of failure) and serving-without-gpu; the Analyzer returns a diversity-vs-cost Pareto front.

zen_mapping.freedom: 3 worker slots from 3 instance types, repetition allowed

oracle: FW_VAR=2 zero diversity (all slots same type); FW_VAR=3 serving without a gpu slot; FW_VAR=0 safe (codes kept small to fit combo-column capacity)

teaching_summary: User problem (resource allocation multiset (FW_CombiR)). Ran 20 candidates: 12x PASS (safe allocation), 6x zero diversity: all 3 slots same type (single point of failure), 2x serving workload allocated no gpu slot. Formal Pareto front of 6. Verbs: 3 worker slots from 3 instance types, repetition allowed -> FW_CombiR(3); workload class -> FW_Combi(1); resource-mix policy -> TAIL oracle (FW_VAR). NOTE: 3 of 6 Pareto-front candidates are DOMAIN_FAIL (findings, not deployable): the formal front is over ALL executed candidates; DOMAIN_FAIL members are findings, not deployable — pick the best PASS candidate to deploy.
